note: Salesforce Soap exposes exactly one service, salesforce.soap_client (Drupal\salesforce_soap\Soap\SoapClient), wrapping the Salesforce SOAP Partner API and authenticating via the suite's auth-provider manager. It has NO config, permissions, plugins or Drush of its own. Therefore the only local, verifiable state relevant to this module is (a) that its service is registered and (b) the suite's default auth provider the SOAP client authenticates with (salesforce.settings.salesforce_auth_provider). One medium introspects the service's presence; the other medium and both hard cases exercise salesforce_auth_provider (shared suite config, framed from the SOAP client's perspective), verified by pure reads. Cleanup restores salesforce_auth_provider to '' and leaves the module enabled (campaign baseline). Real SOAP calls need ext-soap + a live org and are out of scope.

evals.prompt: What does the Salesforce Soap module provide, and how would I use it from code?
evals.expected_output: It provides the salesforce.soap_client service (Drupal\salesforce_soap\Soap\SoapClient) that wraps the Salesforce SOAP (Partner) API. Get it with \Drupal::service('salesforce.soap_client') or inject it; it has no config of its own.

evals.prompt: How does the Salesforce SOAP client authenticate - does it need its own credentials configuration?
evals.expected_output: No separate config: the SOAP client authenticates through the same auth-provider system as REST (plugin.manager.salesforce.auth_providers), using a salesforce_auth authorization and the suite default salesforce.settings.salesforce_auth_provider.

evals.prompt: What are the prerequisites/limits of the Salesforce Soap module - does it add configuration or permissions, and what PHP extension does it require?
evals.expected_output: It requires the PHP ext-soap extension and adds no configuration, permissions, plugins, or Drush - it is a pure service that reuses the suite's authorization.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is the Salesforce SOAP client service available? Inspect the site and give the service id if present.
evals.expected_output: Yes: the salesforce.soap_client service is registered (the SoapClient wrapping the Salesforce SOAP Partner API).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, which Salesforce authorization will the SOAP client authenticate with (the suite's default provider)? Inspect the live Salesforce settings and give the id.
evals.expected_output: It uses soap_prod: salesforce.settings.salesforce_auth_provider = soap_prod, which the SOAP client (like REST) authenticates with.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, make the Salesforce SOAP client (and the rest of the suite) authenticate using the authorization with id soap_auth by setting it as the default Salesforce auth provider. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: salesforce.settings.salesforce_auth_provider is set to soap_auth (the authorization the SOAP client uses).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the default Salesforce authorization (used by the SOAP client) is set to old_soap. Repoint it to the authorization soap_sandbox. Apply the change to the live site.
